title: In all thy ways (Berakhot 63a, Proverbs 3:6)
hook: "In all thy ways acknowledge Him", a short verse on which the whole Torah hangs
tomorrow: everyone grabs the fun jobs. who does the rest?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the fox and the fish, and Akiva's answer to fear: water is our life. Today, one small verse that some sages said the whole of that water hangs on.

The kettle clicks off. Steam on your face. A warm mug in both hands. Nobody would call that a religious moment. The Talmud might. Bar Kappara, a sage, asks a question in Berakhot: what is the small passage that all the main parts of the Torah depend on? He doesn't pick a commandment or a story. He picks one line from Proverbs, and it's about mugs, more or less.
screen: `THE KETTLE. THE STEAM. THE MUG.` → `WHAT DOES IT ALL HANG ON?` → `ONE LINE FROM PROVERBS.`

segments.voice: Here it is, in the old Jewish translation: "In all thy ways acknowledge Him, and He will direct thy paths." In Hebrew, b'khol d'rakhekha da'ehu. Da'ehu means know Him. Not only in the synagogue, not only on holy days. In all your ways: the walk to the bus, the dishes, the mug. Why would that be the hinge of everything? Because every other commandment happens somewhere. At a table, in a field, in a store, at a door. This verse says the somewhere itself is where God is known. It turns the whole day into the place, not just the parts with prayers in them. Then Rava, another sage, adds something startling: even in a matter of wrongdoing. Readers explain that line in different ways. One plain reading: there's no corner of life the verse doesn't reach, not even the corners you're not proud of. You don't step out of God's sight to do the wrong thing. Something to tell a friend tonight: this is the same tractate whose blessings you've been learning all along, for food, for a scent, for a place, for standing up. Bar Kappara's verse is the reason behind all of them. Each blessing is a way of knowing God in one small way, one act at a time, through the hands, the nose, the tongue. The mug counts.
screen: `ACKNOWLEDGE HIM: KNOW HIM.` · `EVERY COMMANDMENT HAPPENS SOMEWHERE.` · `RAVA: EVEN THE CORNERS.` · `WHY EVERY BLESSING EXISTS.` · then, large: `IN ALL THY WAYS.`

segments.voice: Pour yourself something to drink, water or tea, and hold it before you sip. Feel the temperature in your hands, smell it, then taste it slowly. As you do, acknowledge God in the act, with the verse, in your own words, or in silence.
In all thy ways. Bar Kappara's small verse from Proverbs: know God not only in prayer, but in every road you walk.
The line to keep: in all thy ways, the mug and the bus and the dishes included. Day forty-three of fifty in Berakhot.

screen: `DAY 1530 COUNTS.` → `BERAKHOT · 43 OF 50.` → `TOMORROW: EVERYONE GRABS THE FUN JOBS. WHO DOES THE REST?`

howItsDone: In Jewish practice a short blessing comes before eating or drinking, and morning and evening prayers frame the day; teachers quote Proverbs 3:6 for the idea behind them: God known in ordinary acts.
